newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice sues states over female inmate rapes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice sues states over female inmate rapes.

text.p: The Justice Department sued Arizona and Michigan Monday alleging that female inmates at their state-run prisons have been subjected to unlawful invasions of privacy and sexual assaults by guards.

The lawsuits seek a court order requiring that the two states protect female inmates from rape, sexual assault or other improper sexual contact by prison staff and ensure that inmates and staff do not engage in sexual relations.
The department also said it would seek to ensure that female inmates were not improperly viewed when showering, changing or using toilet facilities.

The department began looking at the two state-run women's prisons in Michigan, which hold more than 1,200 inmates, in 1994 after complaints about alleged sexual misconduct. It received complaints about three female correctional facilities in Arizona, which hold some 1,000 inmates, early in 1995.

Department officials said both states refused to cooperate in the investigation and a settlement could not be reached. The lawsuits, filed in federal court in Phoenix and Detroit, were brought under a 1980 civil rights law aimed at protecting the rights of people housed in state and local government institutions, including prisons.
